title: CUDA Out of Memory
description: Troubleshooting and resolving CUDA Out of Memory (OOM) errors in PyTorch.
name: CUDA Out of Memory

symptoms.symptom: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate...
symptoms.description: The program halts during the forward or backward pass with a PyTorch traceback stating CUDA OOM, indicating that total active allocations exceeded hardware GPU RAM capacity.

root_causes.explanation: Accumulating activation tensors for backpropagation exceeds the available memory capacity on the configured GPU hardware.

Storing training output tensors containing gradient tracking history in global variables or lists (e.g. logging history without calling loss.item()) prevents the garbage collector from freeing memory.

diagnosis.expected_result: Active memory allocation values dropping when garbage collection is called.
diagnosis.how_to_perform: Use print(torch.cuda.memory_summary(device=None, abbreviated=False)) directly before and after garbage collection runs.

steps: Halve the batch size value (e.g., from 64 to 32).
Enable gradient accumulation step adjustments to compensate for loss representation constraints.
solutions.verification: Rerun training execution loop. Verify that epochs complete without traceback warnings.

practices: Employ torch.utils.checkpoint during model configuration to discard intermediate activations and recalculate them during backward steps.
Regularly call torch.cuda.empty_cache() between validation cycles to flush fragmented blocks back to the GPU allocator.
